body_markdown:
# Introduction

This final assessment reviews skills practised across the 365-day plan. It is a self-check, not an official certification. Complete the sections honestly and note which areas need more practice.

## 1. Grammar

Choose the correct answer:

1. She ___ English every day. (practises / practise)
2. They ___ finished the task. (have / has)
3. I ___ at home yesterday. (was / were)
4. He is interested ___ learning. (in / on)
5. The email ___ sent this morning. (was / were)

## 2. Vocabulary

Match the word to its meaning:

1. reliable
2. assist
3. urgent
4. improve
5. confirm

a. make better
b. needing quick attention
c. make sure something is correct
d. help
e. can be trusted

## 3. Reading

Read: “Ravi wanted to improve his English. He spent fifteen minutes each day reading, listening and speaking. At first, he made mistakes and paused often. After several weeks, he could explain familiar topics more clearly. He continued practising because he knew that regular effort was important.”

Questions:
1. What did Ravi want to improve?
2. How much time did he practise each day?
3. Name two activities he did.
4. What changed after several weeks?
5. Why did he continue?

## 4. Listening

Ask a partner to read this twice, or use text-to-speech:

“The office will remain closed on Sunday. Employees should complete their weekly reports by Saturday afternoon. For urgent matters, contact the duty manager.”

Questions:
1. Which day will the office be closed?
2. When should reports be completed?
3. Whom should employees contact for urgent matters?

## 5. Speaking

Speak for one minute on each topic:
- Introduce yourself and your background.
- Describe your daily routine.
- Explain a task you know well.
- Talk about a goal you want to achieve.

## 6. Writing

Write a paragraph of 80 to 100 words about how you use English in daily life. Include what you can do confidently and what you still want to improve.

## Answer key

Grammar: 1 practises, 2 have, 3 was, 4 in, 5 was.

Vocabulary: 1-e, 2-d, 3-b, 4-a, 5-c.

Reading: 1 English. 2 Fifteen minutes. 3 Any two: reading, listening, speaking. 4 He explained familiar topics more clearly. 5 He knew regular effort was important.

Listening: 1 Sunday. 2 By Saturday afternoon. 3 The duty manager.

## Progress review

Rate yourself from 1 to 5 in grammar, vocabulary, reading, listening, speaking and writing. Choose the lowest two scores and plan four weeks of focused practice.

faq.question: How should I use this lesson?
faq.answer: Complete each activity in order, check the answer key and repeat the speaking or writing task.

faq.question: What should I do if I make mistakes?
faq.answer: Review the explanation, correct your answer and practise the skill again. Mistakes are part of learning.
